notes: Route: expansion.mx robots.txt is permissive (only /busqueda, /buscador, /cms/, /*page=, preview/auth paths and *.rss/*.atom are disallowed) and names https://expansion.mx/sitemap.xml, a sitemapindex of 8 shards. Fetched the index (200) then sitemap1..8.xml (all 200): sitemap1..7 are old archive chunks, 34k-50k locs each, contributing 8 in-window URLs between them; sitemap8.xml (48,654 locs) holds the recent archive and covers the whole window. Every article URL carries the publication date in its path /<section>/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>, which equals the entry's <lastmod> and the page JSON-LD datePublished (verified 6 re-fetches: /bespoke-ad/2026/09/25/, /bespoke-ad/2026/09/30/, /opinion/2026/10/01/, /empresas/2026/09/30/, /empresas/2026/10/20/ x2 -> all 200, 4.5k-10k chars of text, |datePublished - listed date| = 0 days; datePublished is UTC so evening posts can read one day later). Unioned with /news-sitemap.xml (200, ~48h only) and /rss (200, 43 items) as a safety net for a lagging shard; both added 0 new rows because sitemap8 already had them. Result: 633 unique URLs, 31/31 days covered, run time 9.5 s, 10 requests. Day counts: 2026-09-30 = 34, 2026-10-20 = 32, but 2026-10-10 = 2, hence low_volume. The 10-10 figure is real, not a broken route: it is a Saturday and the whole window shows the same weekly shape in two independent fields (URL-path date and sitemap <lastmod> agree: Sat 09-26=4, Sun 09-27=2, Sat 10-03=7, Sun 10-04=3, Sat 10-10=2, Sun 10-11=2, Sat 10-17=6, Sun 10-18=1, Sat 10-24=9, Sun 10-25=4, weekdays 20-38), so the outlet simply publishes almost nothing at weekends. Routes tried and closed: /sitemap-2026-10-10.xml, /sitemap/2026/10, /arc/outboundfeeds/sitemap-index/, /feed all 404; /sitemap9.xml and /sitemap10.xml 404 (no shards beyond the index); Wayback CDX for the domain on 2026-10-10 answered 503, so it was not usable; GDELT DOC API returned no response. Script is idempotent (atomic tmp+rename, keyed by URL) and re-runs in ~10 s.
